what_IS_data_today: KERNEL SELECTION. spec/plans/*.plan.json is read by tools/hide_plan.py and applied to the runtime with NO RECOMPILATION -- the binary is untouched between the two runs. Swapping default.plan.json for serial-family.plan.json flips HAWKING_QWEN38_RECON_FUSE from 1 to 0 and HAWKING_DN_RMSNORM_TG from 256 to 512, and generation stays token-identical.
what_is_NOT_data: RESIDENCY. The plan file carries a residency section and it is DECLARATIVE ONLY -- the file says so in its own is_this_actually_data field. G085 measured the artifact at 13.9% of RAM with the pressure crossover 5.2x beyond the model's maximum context, so the runtime hardcodes unified memory and exposes no knob to change it. A plan file whose residency half looks authoritative while being inert would be worse than one that admits it.

THE_VERIFY_IS_NOT_MET.asked: swap plan file, show DIFFERENT DISPATCH CENSUS, same tokens
THE_VERIFY_IS_NOT_MET.got: 964 dispatches under both plans; tokens identical
THE_VERIFY_IS_NOT_MET.why: Every knob the runtime exposes is a kernel SWAP at constant count, not a plan change that adds or removes dispatches. G107 measured the same thing independently -- RECON_FUSE=0 selects different kernel family NAMES at a constant 964. A census that does not move is exactly what a same-count swap should produce.
THE_VERIFY_IS_NOT_MET.and_a_second_limit_worth_stating: the runtime reports a dispatch COUNT but not per-dispatch NAMES, so this cannot independently prove different kernels ran. The evidence that RECON_FUSE selects a different family is the SOURCE (its comment states it selects the G023 serial family names), not the telemetry. Source-verified is weaker than measured and is labelled as such.
